An alien alliance known as the Covenant has invaded human space, destroying our worlds and decimating our fleets.

Above the glassed human colony of Promise orbits a massive Covenant research ship—a prize that the UNSC hopes will point the way to the Covenant home world—and ultimately to victory for humanity.

>>BEGIN TRANSCRIPTION



Erudition Log / Nineteenth Cycle, Seventh Unit

Inward Scrutiny codified aboard <i>Triumph of Tolerance</> by the hand of the Inquisitive Technologist Minister of Harmony



Failure. It is a necessary, inevitable aspect of progress.

It is like faith, in that way. The path of the Great Journey is not a direct line of transit, but many winding roads that weave through moments of clarity and crisis—separating for a time before eventually coming together again.

From the testimonies that fill the Record of Punished Deeds, our people know this well. Our ancient ancestors were fortunate to have had the guiding wisdom of the Oracle of Oracles in their time, teaching us to harness our potential as we explored and mastered our natal world. I have always been fascinated by the texts which speak of the Former Age, for so much of it is lost to us now. Passages speak of the gods’ command over genetics, the biological customization of their divine forms to suit their hallowed purposes.

Alas, the Oracle remains silent at the heart of our holy city now. We have been set on the path, but we must walk it ourselves.

The Jiralhanae proved to be most interesting test subjects for experimentation. As young initiates to the Covenant, lifted from the ashes and wastes of their homeworld, many of their young are filled with the glorious gift of purpose now that they are no longer pitted against their own kind in petty wars over territorial disputes.

I am truly inspired by their newfound belief. So often, it is only through the eyes of our newest converts that we can recall and renew our own spiritual fervor that can be sublimated by time and duty. The Jiralhanae’s addition to the Covenant could not have come at a more fortuitous time, and I expect great use shall be made of them in the cycles to come. There is plenty of time yet to determine their genetic refinement for the future and how I shall sculpt their minds and bodies to best serve our will.

I must convene with the Minister of Preparation once the data from this endeavor has been thoroughly analyzed, for I am certain that his chirurgeons will take great interest in this research as their work to unlock the potential of our own species continues in earnest.

I have missed the Gardens of Reverent Contemplation. Yes, a lunar cycle of restitution and reconnection shall be of great benefit to me.

Perhaps a visit to the Sacred Promissory is in order. I am most curious to see how the latest developments of our fighting skins are manifesting.

I must hasten, for it is time to depart. The Demon has done his work to desecrate my beautiful <i>Triumph of Tolerance</>, but I eagerly await the time that we may bring the fullest might of the San’Shyuum to bear.

Until the coming of that glorious day.

Erudition Log / Tenth Cycle, Fourth Unit

Inward Scrutiny codified aboard <i>Triumph of Tolerance</> by the hand of the Inquisitive Technologist Minister of Harmony



Blessed are the ways in which we walk. Aimed towards the bright sun of progress, with the shadow of complacency at our back and out of view. Our endeavor towards perfection is a great journey all its own, and may we never lose our way from its Path.

These are words I must recite at the dawn of each passing cycle, that I might not find myself encumbered by piety of policy alone.

There is a seed of fervor planted deep within my heart, tended well by the soil of my soul. I will nurture it until it bears the fruit I seek—sweet flesh that will redefine our understanding of the divine.

There is much we were made for, and much we can make of ourselves. But there is also that which we can make of others. It is of paramount importance that we vouchsafe our ability to maintain order—to stride forward with command and confidence, that our kind might illuminate the path of those to follow.

I have spent much time in the texts of ancient ways, enlightened even by what some might call apocrypha. I devour every stroke, every syllable—each page turning from intimation to revelation to invitation.

Our kind was once masters of the code of life—geneweavers whose beauty knew no bounds, and whose abilities were carried by their ambitions. We arranged the proteins and structures of the cell like dipping our quills in an ever-flowing well of ink, writing new forms upon the page as poetry. Hearts beat at our behest, muscles danced at our desire, and it must be this way again.

The old ways must be made new, to make a now that lives eternal. When I spoke with the High Prophet of Truth to make blessed our commissioning, I wished for my wonder to be woven with wisdom. But I do not know if the Hierarchs hear me. Were I to sit in their place, I would sew tightly our empire with the thread of influence. My work has the possibility to give us greater control than we have ever known before. I must prove its worth—my worth.

We are on the precipice of victory against those we trample underfoot, but even our enemies can be useful. Squeezed and juiced that their pulp might serve our whim and way.

Our victory at Fergea will make an ideal place to conduct my next tests. I have new ideas I need to put through their appropriate paces. New hypotheses to turn from theory to law. The universe begs to be commanded—longs for the opportunity to serve a greater voice.

I must simply find the right words for us to speak.

>>DATA TRANSCRIPTION ANALYSIS - FILE EXTRACTION SUCCESSFUL

>>BEGIN TRANSCRIPTION



MONITOR REPORT

[alpha site]

04-343



<i>“We deserve to be forgotten.”</>

Those were the final words imparted to me by 049 Abject Testament before we were assigned to our respective installations and went our separate ways.

I have had [5,527,560 hours] to ponder and reflect on that [dictum], and to this day I am yet to arrive at my own conclusion. And I feel that I must reach some kind of consensus, for this will surely impact my own perspective on my duties as caretaker. Perhaps I may benefit from a good rhetorical exercise.

There is so little that I can remember about the time before I was assigned to my installation. But I remember the Librarian and the lessons she sought to impart.

She said that we are honored with life, and all have our part to play in [Living Time], and so we must perceive and understand the consequences of our actions. If we do not, then we are forced to live them again—around another corner, from another angle. History shall circle back upon us again and again, until we are eventually humbled with wisdom.

And oh, how my makers have been humbled!

Yet, there are many things that I have forgotten in order to best serve the role of monitor for Installation 04.

My past, who I was before accepting my [present duties], is gone from me. Perhaps it still exists under multiple layers of [anamnesis]. Sometimes, I think pieces of it may seep through the gaps in my compartmentalization—no process is perfect, after all. But my makers wisely limited my knowledge and provided me with all that I require to maintain [alpha site].

Perhaps to [obliviate] is—at times—a necessary function. It is, after all, a fundamental trait of organic beings, at least of those recorded in my experiences and archived records.

Is there not a danger in organic beings’ propensity to venerate the imperative to remember as a moral obligation without truly paying heed to the lessons of that history? My makers suffered greatly from this in their waning millennia as the Builder rate closed its grip on the [central government], exalting the alleged glory of the past while casting the then-present as [aberrant]. With the continued lapse of [Alexandria before the Fire] from this age, I fear that future civilizations will not be able to [apprentice themselves] from our deep well of history.

What must we look like to the young species we indexed for the Conservation Measure? Did they look to us as [gods]—as divine beings sheltering them on our [Waypoint] as a threat beyond their comprehension drowned whole worlds and star systems across the galaxy? Do they see the power of our advanced [ordnance] and wish to claim that for themselves?

Ah, but my mind is wandering now. Yes, there are benefits indeed to both remembrance and forgetting, I could spend many cycles detailing the virtues and shortcomings of both. Perhaps I shall to pass some time, if it proves necessary.

But the question is: do we deserve to be forgotten?

Did 049 Abject Testament mean this to be a blessing or punishment for our people after the activation of the [destructive arrayed matrix]?

Was our [pyrrhic measurement] to save the galaxy a crime so great that it should be lost to time—that future civilizations would go without ever knowing of the sacrifice that was made so that they too could one day walk among the stars?

And what of [those who are chosen] to reclaim my makers’ Mantle of Responsibility? If the plan succeeds, are they condemned to repeat the same mistakes of the past? They are, after all, so very similar to each other...

Hmm, it seems like I will not arrive at an answer today. I shall dedicate further consideration to this topic over the [ages] to come. According to protocol, the first scheduled status update from my fellow monitors is due in just [1,217,640 hours]. I hope that I will be able to gain further clarity from 049 Abject Testament himself when the time comes.

>>DATA TRANSCRIPTION ANALYSIS - FILE EXTRACTION SUCCESSFUL

>>BEGIN TRANSCRIPTION



MONITOR REPORT: FIRST SUMMIT

[alpha site]

04-343



Oh, what an exciting occasion! According to protocol, today marks the first scheduled status update from the other installations.

Of course, I am tempering my excitement with a reminder that we are still [bereft] of [Alexandria before the Fire], and so we must utilize wormhole-based superluminal communications, for which the [bandwidth latency] of the sheer amount of shared data is especially cumbersome.

There are faster methods, of course.
